cue: The view is a wide ring of soft light. Ultraviolet, blue and green are shown in false colour, and the picture runs a little slower than yours, then jumps ahead.

cpd.note: highest detail a honeybee worker resolves

fov.note: whole-animal horizontal field, a general bee figure

fovea.note: no sharp middle is drawn beyond the zone below

rate.note: slows the picture so that a bee's faster flicker sight can be felt

living.note: no extra weight for living movement

sat.note: keeps colour as a person sees it, apart from the false colour map

rows: A honeybee resolves detail only as fine as about a quarter of a grating cycle per degree, roughly one two-hundredth of what a person sees. Its middle is no sharper than its edge, so the picture stays soft all over.
A bee sees close to the whole way round, with a small blind region behind and below. The view is squeezed to fit a wide field.

Bees have three kinds of colour receptor, in ultraviolet, blue and green, so they see ultraviolet which people cannot. This view shows ultraviolet as blue, blue as green and green as red, and drops red, because bees do not see far red.
bee.jsonl:German Aerospace Center (DLR) and Bee Sensory and Behavioural Ecology Lab 2026
A bee sees flicker faster than people do, up to about 200 times a second in bright light. Its picture is reported to be faster than ours, so this view moves more slowly to suggest the difference.
A bee turns its head in quick jumps of 5 to 60 degrees, then holds its view still between jumps.
The glow, its colour, the gain, the speed of the picture, the wide soft ring and the false colour grid are the app's own choices to make the bee's view easy to picture. No record gives these numbers.
